card.title: 18. INFANTRY REGIMENT
card.text: Deployment: Moves into the frontline if possible.
card.flavorText: Formed in Bielefeld in 1934, the 18th Infantry Regiment became one of three main infantry regiments within the German 6th Infantry Division. Initially composed of three battalions, the 18th Regiment contributed men and officers to other formations as the war progressed. In late 1940, its headquarters and third battalion were transferred to help form the 106th Infantry Division, a common practice as the German Army expanded its frontlines. The 6th Infantry Division itself was one of the Wehrmacht’s early peacetime formations, mobilized in August 1939 for the invasion of Poland. Alongside the 18th, it included the 37th and 58th Infantry Regiments, supported by Artillery Regiment 6. The division fought across Europe and later on the Eastern Front, enduring heavy losses. By 1942, all German infantry regiments were redesignated as “Grenadier” regiments, but this change had no effect on their actual structure or role. In October 1943, the division was reorganized into a leaner “neuer Art” format, reflecting reduced manpower. In June 1944, it was encircled and destroyed during the Soviet Union’s massive Operation Bagration. The 6th Infantry Division was officially dissolved shortly after.
